When we mounted the filesystem after the crash
message:
BTRFS error (device xxx): block group xxxx has wrong amount of free space
BTRFS error (device xxx): failed to load free space cache for block group xxx
It is because we didn't update the metadata of the allocated space (in extent
tree) until the file data was written into the disk. During this time
no information about the allocated spaces in either the extent tree nor the
free space cache. when we wrote out the free space cache at this time (commit
transaction)
column2: those spaces were lost. In fact
column3: only the free space that is

column1: used to store the file data had this problem
the metadata of them is updated in the same transaction context.
There are many methods which can fix the above problem
- track the allocated space
column2: and write it out when we write out the free

column1: space cache
- account the size of the allocated space that is used to store the file
data
column2: if the size is not zero
column3: don't write out the free space cache.

column1: The first one is complex and may make the performance drop down.
This patch chose the second method
column2: we use a per-block-group variant to

column1: account the size of that allocated space. Besides that
a per-block-group read-write semaphore to avoid the race between
the allocation and the free space cache write out.
